requirement:
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Every obligation in `requirements.references.outlines` has code and a test.

**Obligations and the code that carries them out**
- **Pinned grammars for the seven languages.** `parse_redacted` in `src/outline/mod.rs` loads each profile's grammar with a tree-sitter `Parser`. `Cargo.toml` pins every `tree-sitter*` crate with an exact `=` version.
- **Extension selection, case-insensitive.** `profile_for_path` in `src/outline/profile.rs` lowercases the extension and searches `profiles()`. `parse` (`src/outline/mod.rs`) calls it. `parse_with` takes a profile that callers select the same way. `OutlineCache::parse` in `src/inputs.rs`, which `outline` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` reaches through `sources.parse_file`, also calls it.
  - Test: `profiles_are_selected_by_extension_case_insensitively`.
- **A syntax error fails the parse and reports the first error's line.** `check_errors` walks the tree in document order and returns an `OutlineError` carrying the line of the first `ERROR` or missing node. `parse_redacted` calls it before building anything.
  - Test: `reports_parse_failures_with_lines`, which covers Rust, Python and TOML. It asserts the reported line is the first error (line 3 where a later error exists) and that the message starts with `line 3:`. The check is shared across languages, so one test of the common path is enough.
- **Plain-text profile.** `plain_text` in `src/outline/mod.rs` emits one anonymous `line` node per non-blank line and skips blank lines. `plain::PROFILE` is the fallback when no extension matches.
  - Test: `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes`.
- **Per-language profile mapping.** Each file (`rust.rs`, `python.rs`, `typescript.rs`, `css.rs`, `markdown.rs`, `toml.rs`, `yaml.rs`) has a `KINDS` table of `KindRule`s. Each rule maps a grammar kind to an outline kind with a `NameRule`: `Anonymous`, `Field`, `FirstChild` or `Custom`. Together these state named-or-anonymous and by which field or child.
  - Tests: one per language, i.e. `python_profile_outlines_defs_classes_and_statements`, `typescript_profile_outlines_declarations`, `css_profile_names_rules_by_normalized_selectors`, `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` and `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys`. Rust is covered by the tools outline test and the other Rust tests in `src/outline/tests.rs`.
- **Only mapped kinds appear, other nodes are transparent, and comments are never nodes.** In `Builder::walk`, `maps` excludes comment nodes. Unmapped nodes recurse with the same parent, so their outline descendants land under the nearest outline ancestor.
- **Attached siblings.** The `attaches` hook, used by Rust for attributes and outer doc comments and by Python for decorators, feeds the attached nodes into `line_start` and the hashes in `finish`.
- **Root node, and no fallback kinds.** `root_node` always creates node 0 covering the whole file. Unmapped top-level code stays in the root, and the profiles define no fallback kinds.
  - Tests: `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` and `no_profile_invents_fallback_kinds`.
- **Profiles are documented.** `md/reference.md` has an "Outline profiles" table and "Profile details". Its rows match the `KINDS` tables I read, and its extensions match `rust.rs`, `typescript.rs`, `css.rs`, `markdown.rs` and `yaml.rs`. The `python.rs` and `toml.rs` tables were not read.
- **Upgrading is deliberate.** Exact version pins in `Cargo.toml`, plus the paragraph in `md/reference.md` stating that upgrading a grammar or changing a profile is a deliberate change.
- **Outline tool.** `outline` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` returns the nested outline entries. Its test is `outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs`.
- **Redaction does not change the outline.** `redaction_never_changes_an_outline` in `src/redaction/tests.rs` checks this.

**Other `{impl}` items.** `innermost_at_line` and `node_lines` are covered by `line_queries_find_innermost_nodes` and other outline tests. The `Debug` impl for `Profile` just writes the profile name and adds no unspecified behavior.

**Note on Markdown.** The anonymous section before the first heading is a mapped grammar kind (`section`) that the documented table lists. It is not an invented fallback kind.

None of these obligations needs an exemption from testing, and no `{fixme}` references are involved.
